quote_text:
The manager said that was the worst  performance of his time. What went wrong today? 
I think that’s a very good question — a very  difficult one to answer for me right now,  
just after the game and still high in emotion. I  think we need to do a good analysis, but overall,  
what my feeling is — I think we didn’t play enough  of our football. We didn’t stress them enough,  
didn’t give them enough difficult moments,  and they used their moments very well.
Where do you go from here in terms of  trying to get some kind of reaction? 
Yeah, that’s the hard thing, but also  the good thing about being at a club  
like Rangers — you have to bounce back.  It’s not like you don’t have a choice.
Wednesday again, we have a very difficult and  important game. We have to bounce back. We don’t  
have a choice. I think as a team, we need to stick  together now. Probably you guys have heard this  
before already, and I think today on the pitch  we didn’t stick together enough. But definitely  
in the next days, we will need that if we want a  good performance — and we want that on Wednesday.
Philippe Clement said there  was a nervousness about the  
team today — the display today — that he hadn’t  seen coming. Did you recognize that nervousness? 
For me on the pitch, I think it’s hard to  say. Like I said, I just came off the pitch,  
and I see the game differently.
But I think that we were not calm enough — yeah,  
I can agree with that. We didn’t shift the  ball enough, go from side to side, try to  
open up their block and then play through it.  We were a little bit — yeah, impatient at times.
And I think we need that in our game, especially  in these kinds of games, to stretch their block  
and then find the spaces in between with the  quality we have there, with the midfielders,  
to then turn the game and create something. I  was maybe sometimes a little bit too direct.
But yeah, we will need to make that analysis.
The manager said there has to be more  leadership. Would you agree with that? 
Yeah, definitely. That’s also something I take  on myself as one of the more experienced players.
I think we try to — for me, I think Tav, Jacko,  
we all try that. But I think it can  always be better — be more convincing,  
more motivating to the whole team, also  to the younger guys, to take them with us.
We’ve had these moments in our careers,  these games, and it’s about just taking  
them with us in these moments and pulling  them through the hard moments in a game.
And then maybe you get the goal,  
or you get the one-nil in your advantage.  So yeah, I think I can agree with that.
A lot of fans are talking about the manager — they  want a change. What would you say about Philippe  
Clement’s position? Why should he be the manager? I think it’s very difficult for me to speak  
about that topic. But I think for us — the  manager prepared the game the whole week.
We trained on certain things during the week,  
and if I look at today, I think we  didn’t execute these things enough.
So, yeah, I try to look at what I can control and  
focus on the team and the players. I  think today is below our standards.
Do you think the players have  let the manager down today? 
I don’t think so. I think — I think nobody  of us has that in his mind. I think we’re  
letting ourselves down, I think we’re  letting the club down, the fans down.
Obviously, we’ve said this a few times in  the last months, and I think, just for us,  
for ourselves, we need a big performance.  We need to straighten our backs so that we  
don’t have to apologize anymore to the  fans for these kinds of performances.
We saw so many fans leaving after 70  minutes. They didn’t believe the team could  
get back into the game. How does that feel? Yeah, that hurts. But I think somewhere,  
yeah, we can understand it.
The last home game was a very tough one. We  wanted to bounce back partly, but we wanted  
to bounce back today — show them something,  give them something — and clearly, we didn’t.
So there is an understanding for that situation,  and like I say, it’s time for us to stick together  
and hopefully reach a point where we don’t need to  make these apologies anymore in the near future.
Do you feel you have something to  prove here? Do you feel you need to  
show the fans that these players belong here? 
That’s a hard question. I think these players  have already shown that they belong at a club  
like Rangers — all of them. They have  the quality to be at a club like Rangers.
But it’s more than quality alone. I think, for me,  
quality is also showing it consistently on a  weekly basis — and at Rangers, twice a week.
That’s real quality because you can say talent  is technical ability and all this, but for me,  
it’s about showing it every week.
We need to make a step there as a group —  to show it twice a week — the real quality,  
the real mentality. And I’m  talking about technical,  
tactical, the mentality, and  the physical side of things.
There are still steps to be made there.
Thank you, Cyriel. Thank you.
title: 'It hurt to see fans leaving.' FULL Cyriel Dessers Post Match Interview | Rangers 0-2 St Mirren
